html:
A novel by Fyodor Dostoevsky, published in monthly parts in 1866. It follows a murderer's conscience from the inside and is a landmark of psychological fiction.

Raskolnikov is a poor former student in Saint Petersburg. He talks himself into the idea that some extraordinary people, like Napoleon, have the right to break moral laws for a higher purpose. To prove it he kills an old pawnbroker with an axe.

Most of the book comes after the crime. Raskolnikov is torn by fever, fear and guilt, and plays a cat and mouse game with a clever police investigator, Porfiry. He is drawn to Sonya, a young woman forced into prostitution to feed her family, whose quiet faith offers him a way back. In the end he confesses and is sent to Siberia.

The novel was written fast, while Dostoevsky was deep in debt. It attacks the radical ideas of young Russians of the 1860s and shaped later writers and thinkers, from the existentialists to crime fiction.
sum: A novel by Fyodor Dostoevsky, published in monthly parts in 1866. It follows a murderer's conscience from the inside and is a landmark of psychological fiction.
